title: PWS obs message, contract v2
description: Observation records published by the gateway on V2/{user_id}/PWS/{device_id}/obs (QoS 1, not retained). In contract v2 the gateway is the weather station: it combines every sensor it hears into ONE record per bucket, so there is no per station array. Each record says whether it was sent live or backfilled and whether the gateway clock was synced when it was recorded. Delivery is at least once: the server dedupes on (device_id, bucket start rounded down to interval_s). The payload version is 2 and is not accepted on the old pws/ topics; the old shape (v 0, obs.schema.json) is not accepted on the V2 topics.

v.description: Payload version. Always 2 for this schema. This is how the server tells the two obs shapes apart.

device_id.description: Publishing device. Must match the device_id in the topic.

seq.description: Monotonic message sequence number per device, used for dedupe and gap detection. Never reused within a firmware install.

sent.description: Time the message was handed to the MQTT client, UTC. May be much later than the bucket starts when the outbox is replaying.

interval_s.description: Length of each bucket in seconds, for example 300. All buckets in a message share this interval. A bucket start is aligned to it.

buckets.description: Records in ascending start order, oldest first, each with the station's own timestamp. A backfill sends at most 20 per message; a message never exceeds 64 KB, so the device splits by bucket when needed.

record.description: The combined observation of the whole gateway for one bucket.

start.description: Bucket start, UTC, aligned to interval_s. Together with device_id this is the idempotency key: a second record with the same device and the same start is a duplicate and is ignored.

live.description: true when the record was sent in the normal cycle, shortly after its bucket closed. false when it is a backfill: it waited in the outbox (the link was down) or it answers a resync command. The server uses it to treat a late record as history, not as a current reading.

synced.description: true when the gateway clock was synchronized (NTP, GPS, LTE or a trusted RTC) while the bucket was recorded. A gateway never uplinks while unsynced, so false means the bucket was recorded unsynced and the clock has since been corrected, and its timestamps are less trustworthy.

n.description: Number of decoded packets, summed over every sensor that contributed, that went into the bucket. 0 is allowed.

f.description: Canonical fields, see common.schema.json#/$defs/fields. Each field comes from the sensor the owner chose for it on the gateway (see src). A field nobody supplied is absent.

src.description: Which sensor supplied each field in f, for support and display only: canonical field name to the sensor key. The server never needs it to compute anything. Omitted when the gateway has a single sensor.

raw.description: Raw samples kept for the bucket: decoder fields with no canonical mapping, keyed by sensor key, then by the decoder's own field name, unconverted. The server stores this without interpreting it.

meta.description: Site metadata for the combined record. alt_m is the altitude of the sensor that supplied the pressure, wind_height_m the height of the one that supplied the wind. The server derives sea level pressure and 10 m wind from them.

alt_m.description: Altitude of the pressure sensor above mean sea level in metres. Unbounded.

wind_height_m.description: Height of the anemometer above ground in metres. Unbounded.

signal.description: Radio link quality averaged over the sensors that contributed.

rssi_db.description: Received signal strength in dB. Unbounded; driver specific.

snr_db.description: Signal to noise ratio in dB. Unbounded; driver specific.
